theme: 3 terms on class initializers: main, shortcut and must-have

terms.definition: An initializer that sets every property of a class and is the main way to create it.
terms.example: Write a designated initializer, so `Chat` sets every property.

terms.definition: An initializer that is a shortcut and calls another initializer of the same class.

terms.definition: An initializer marked with a keyword that every subclass must also write.
terms.example: Mark it as a required initializer, so every subclass must write it.

video.title: Designated Initializer, Convenience Initializer & Required Initializer | iOS Daily English Day 17
video.description:
Learn to talk about Swift class initializers: Designated Initializer, Convenience Initializer & Required Initializer, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Designated Initializer - An initializer that sets every property of a class and is the main way to create it.
Convenience Initializer - An initializer that is a shortcut and calls another initializer of the same class.
Required Initializer - An initializer marked with a keyword that every subclass must also write.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: Swift Designated, Convenience & Required Initializers in English | Chat | Day 17
landscape.description:
Explain Designated Initializer, Convenience Initializer & Required Initializer in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
지정, 편의, 필수 초기화 메서드 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Designated Initializer - An initializer that sets every property of a class and is the main way to create it.
한국어: 지정 초기화: 클래스의 모든 프로퍼티를 설정하는 기본 초기화 메서드

Convenience Initializer - An initializer that is a shortcut and calls another initializer of the same class.
한국어: 편의 초기화: 같은 클래스의 다른 초기화 메서드를 호출하는 지름길 초기화 메서드

Required Initializer - An initializer marked with a keyword that every subclass must also write.
한국어: 필수 초기화: 모든 서브클래스가 반드시 구현해야 하는 초기화 메서드

dialogue.title: The Chat initializers

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I need a `Chat` that starts with a title.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Write a designated initializer. It sets every property of `Chat`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the designated initializer is `init(title:)`, right?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. Every other initializer must end up calling it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Most chats start with the title "New". I hate typing it every time.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then add a convenience initializer. It calls `init(title:)` with "New".

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh, so a convenience initializer is just a shortcut?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. Now `Chat()` works with no arguments.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Next week I will make a `GroupChat` subclass.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then mark `init(title:)` as a required initializer, so every subclass must write it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good. A required initializer keeps `GroupChat` safe.
